proof:
# Linear cap-distance stability for arbitrary localized corner removals

This is a scoped positive stability theorem for ordinary convex bodies.
It extends the exact truncated-simplex depth law beyond parallel corner
cuts to arbitrary convex bodies whose missing parts stay near simplex
vertices. It also explains an exact two-parameter facet-bump cancellation
after affine simplex changes are removed. General facet-interior or
arbitrary signed body perturbations are not covered.

Let T be a d-simplex, d>=2, with volume V, barycentric functions lambda_i,
m=d+1, Gamma=(d/m)^d, and a_d=Gamma-1/m>0. For full-dimensional bodies
use normalized uniform measures and define

    dist_cap(mu,nu)=sup_(closed halfspaces H)|mu(H)-nu(H)|,
    dist_cap(K,Simp)=inf_(full-dimensional simplices S)
                                      dist_cap(mu_K,mu_S).

The latter quantity already factors all affine simplex changes. It is
not identified with Hausdorff distance or symmetric difference.

## 1. Exact depth depends only on the missing corner volumes

There exists a dimension-only eta_d>0 such that the following holds.
For any convex body K satisfying

    T outside union_i {lambda_i>1-eta_d} subset K subset T,

put

    t_i=|{lambda_i>1-eta_d} outside K|/V,
    t=sum_i t_i=|T outside K|/V.

Choose eta_d<1/2, so these neighborhoods are disjoint. The removed
pieces need not be homothetic simplices, flat cuts, or polyhedral.
Then for all sufficiently small eta_d the exact absolute depth is DV,
where D near Gamma solves

    product_i(D+t_i) [sum_i 1/(D+t_i)]^d=d^d.           (1)

The unique maximizing point has barycentrics

    lambda_i*= [1/(D+t_i)]/[sum_j 1/(D+t_j)],

and the normalized maximum is D/(1-t).

Here is why the changed shape hypothesis is valid. The proof in
`candidate 3795aff5f3322d52`
first localizes ALL maximizing points near the centroid using deletion
mass t, and then localizes ALL minimizing normals near the canonical
apex normals. Those arguments use only K subset T and the total removed
volume. In each resulting normal neighborhood, the entire sufficiently
small i-th vertex neighborhood is strictly included and all other
vertex neighborhoods strictly excluded. Therefore deleting ANY subset
of the i-th neighborhood subtracts exactly t_i V from every such cap.
The local exact depth expression remains

    min_i {d^d product_(j!=i) lambda_j(y)-t_i}.          (2)

The scalar equation and the positive weighted-log-Jensen certificate
then apply without any change. Convexity of K and its retained central
region ensure the same full-dimensional compactness and attainment.
This is an extension by support of the removed sets, not an assertion
that arbitrary small cap-distance perturbations have formula (2).

## 2. A quantitative missing-volume and cap-distance lower bound

After reducing eta_d further if necessary, one has the explicit bound

    D(K)-Gamma >= [a_d t-4t^2/Gamma]/(1-t).             (3)

In particular, if t<=Gamma a_d/8, then

    D(K)-Gamma >= (a_d/2)t
                >= (a_d/2)dist_cap(mu_K,mu_T)
                >= (a_d/2)dist_cap(K,Simp).            (4)

Only the size of the corner neighborhood guaranteeing the normal regime
is implicit. The rate, its coefficient, and its volume cutoff in (3)-(4)
are explicit. No general lower stability modulus is inferred outside
this corner-localized class.

For a direct proof of (3), set b_i=t_i-t/m and choose the candidate

    lambda_i=[1-b_i/Gamma]/m.

The coordinates sum to one, are positive, and are in the neighborhood
where (2) applies when eta_d is small. Also sum |b_i|<=2t. For each i,
the product expansion with x_j=-b_j/Gamma, j!=i, has
S=sum |x_j|<=2t/Gamma. If t<=Gamma/4, then S<=1/2 and

    |product(1+x_j)-1-sum x_j|
      <=sum_(k>=2) S^k/k!
      <=S^2/[2(1-S)]<=S^2.

Since sum_(j!=i)b_j=-b_i, every expression in (2) at this one candidate
is at least Gamma-t/m-4t^2/Gamma. Dividing by 1-t proves (3).
The hypothesis t<=Gamma a_d/8 implies the required t<=Gamma/4 and
makes the numerator in (3) at least (a_d/2)t.

Finally, for K subset T, normalized uniform measures satisfy the EXACT
identity TV(mu_K,mu_T)=t: on the retained K the positive density
difference has total mass t, and the missing part has T mass t.
Halfspaces form a subclass of measurable sets, and T is an admissible
affine simplex comparison. This proves the two last inequalities in (4).
Volume restoration or centroid matching by a common affine map preserves
both D(K) and dist_cap(K,Simp), so it does not remove this conclusion.

The constant a_d is the sharp leading coefficient relative to the missing
volume t, or to cap distance from the FIXED reference T in the one-flat-
corner example. Indeed the exact law gives

    D(K)-Gamma=a_d t+O_d(t^2),

uniformly over corner-volume ratios, and a single flat removed corner
is itself a halfspace trace of T with no K mass, so dist_cap(mu_K,mu_T)=t.
No claim is made that a_d is the best coefficient after the infimum over
ALL affine simplex comparisons, which can make the distance smaller.

## 3. Exact near-vertex facet-bump diagnostic in dimension two

Let T=conv(0,e_1,e_2). For h,k>0 sufficiently small, with k<1, put

    Q_(h,k)=conv(0,e_1,e_2,p), p=(1+h-k,k).

This is a convex quadrilateral, obtained by adding a small outward bump
above the facet x_1+x_2=1. Its area is (1+h)|T|. A cancellation as k
tends to zero might appear to make depth grow much more slowly than
the added area h|T|. The correct affine comparison is instead

    S_(h,k)=conv(0,b e_1,e_2), b=1+h/(1-k).

It contains Q. The ONLY difference is a corner triangle at b e_1, cut
off by the line through e_1 and p. The cut fractions along its two
incident edges are

    r_1=h/(1+h-k), r_2=k,

so the exact missing fraction relative to S is

    tau=r_1 r_2=hk/(1+h-k).                            (5)

As h,k tend to zero independently, both edge fractions tend to zero.
After mapping S to a standard simplex, the entire removed piece is
inside its vertex neighborhood of size max(r_1,r_2). Therefore Section 1
applies despite the fact that this cut is generally NOT parallel to the
opposite facet. The missing corner is itself a halfspace trace, hence

    dist_cap(mu_Q,mu_S)=TV(mu_Q,mu_S)=tau.              (6)

The exact one-corner planar formula gives, throughout this small regime,

    D(Q)=[2(1+sqrt(1+3tau))/9-2tau/3]/(1-tau),
    D(Q)=4/9+tau/9-5tau^2/36+O(tau^3).                (7)

Thus the coordinated cancellation reduces both depth excess and the
cap distance to this affine simplex to order hk. It is not a
counterexample to linear cap-distance stability. In particular (4)
applies to this two-parameter actual convex family, with coefficient
(Gamma_2-1/3)/2=1/18. This calculation does not cover a bump whose
projection stays at a fixed interior point of the facet while h tends
to zero; its removed piece in S then has a long edge fraction, outside
the support condition of Section 1.
